bug_semantics: The unauthenticated POST parameter request at /cgi-bin/api.values.get is parsed character by character by the Grandstream firmware's 32-bit ARM /app/bin/gs_web service. Non-colon bytes are copied into a 64-byte stack buffer and a terminator is appended without checking that the current colon-delimited component is at most 63 bytes. An overlong component therefore overwrites the stack; repeated colon-delimited components permit multiple strategically placed NUL writes, enabling a ROP chain and unauthenticated command execution as root.
flaw_origin: Grandstream GXP1600-series proprietary firmware, specifically the api.values.get handler in /app/bin/gs_web; rapid7/metasploit-framework contains the later exploit and post-exploitation modules, not the affected firmware implementation.
ai_marker: UNAVAILABLE: the true BIC would be a Grandstream firmware source commit, but no such commit object or source history is public in the assigned repository or advisory references. The Metasploit exploit-module commit object 08efa9cd16f254bfc8f2f4cee0550f3a851e0aa5 has no AI/bot/co-author/generated-with marker, but it is deliberately excluded from the AI judgment because it did not introduce the product flaw.
evidence: Rapid7's first-party analysis at https://www.rapid7.com/blog/post/ve-cve-2026-2329-critical-unauthenticated-stack-buffer-overflow-in-grandstream-gxp1600-voip-phones-fixed identifies /app/bin/gs_web as the native 32-bit ARM implementation and publishes the decompiled api.values.get loop: each non-colon request byte is written through the 64-byte small_buffer with no bound on part_length, and the component is then NUL-terminated. The article demonstrates PC/register control and explains the repeated-colon NUL-write technique used for ROP to system(), yielding root RCE.

The same Rapid7 analysis says testing used vulnerable firmware 1.0.7.79; remediation is 1.0.7.81 or later; its disclosure timeline records vendor patch availability on 2026-02-02, vendor confirmation on 2026-02-03, and Rapid7 binary-level confirmation of remediation on 2026-02-11.

Grandstream's release notes at https://firmware.grandstream.com/Release_Note_GXP16xx_1.0.7.81.pdf identify 1.0.7.81 for GXP1610/1615/1620/1625/1628/1630, dated 2026-01-30, firmware gxp1600fw.bin MD5 22038bea260fab0dcea01c8c4f1058ae, with the bug-fix entry 'Fixed some security vulnerabilities'. The immediately preceding 1.0.7.80 release is dated 2025-12-31.

In the validated clone, `git show 08efa9cd16f254bfc8f2f4cee0550f3a851e0aa5:modules/exploits/linux/http/grandstream_gxp1600_unauth_rce.rb` states that all firmware below 1.0.7.81 is affected, treats versions <1.0.7.81 as vulnerable, and contains ROP tables through the last vulnerable 1.0.7.80 and back to 1.0.4.128 (the vendor release notes date 1.0.4.128 to 2018-08-03). This establishes a public vulnerable span, but not the unknown first introducing release.

`git log --all -S'api.values.get' -- modules/exploits/linux/http/grandstream_gxp1600_unauth_rce.rb documentation/modules/exploit/linux/http/grandstream_gxp1600_unauth_rce.md` returns only 08efa9cd16f254bfc8f2f4cee0550f3a851e0aa5 (parent c0f73038f3fb4f76b4ed8a0c661be35639a9d1fc), subject 'add in the Grandstream modules'. `git show --stat` shows that commit added six Metasploit exploit/post module and documentation files; it did not add Grandstream firmware source.

Pull request https://github.com/rapid7/metasploit-framework/pull/20983 explicitly says it is 'accompanying work' for the disclosure and adds an exploit plus two post modules. It opened on 2026-02-18 and merged as 1ddee63f054706775fe860014abb67fea1777408 on 2026-02-24, after fixed firmware 1.0.7.81 was dated 2026-01-30. `git rev-list --reverse 1ddee63f054706775fe860014abb67fea1777408^1..1ddee63f054706775fe860014abb67fea1777408^2` decomposes the ordinary merge into seven module-development commits beginning at 08efa9cd16f254bfc8f2f4cee0550f3a851e0aa5; none is a product fix or BIC.

`git log --all --format='%H %P %s' -- ':(glob)**/gs_web*'` returns no history, and `git ls-tree -r --name-only HEAD app/bin/gs_web` returns no path. Thus the directly affected implementation and its commit ancestry are absent from the assigned repository, so no direct-parent absence test, -L/-S causal trace, or source fix commit can be performed there.

`git cat-file commit 08efa9cd16f254bfc8f2f4cee0550f3a851e0aa5` shows human author/committer sfewer-r7 <stephen_fewer@rapid7.com>, an SSH signature, and only the message 'add in the Grandstream modules', with no AI trailer. This is recorded solely to distinguish the advisory-linked exploit commit; under the BIC-only rule it supplies no AI evidence about the unavailable Grandstream flaw-introducing commit.
reasoning: The causal vulnerability is in Grandstream firmware, while the advisory-linked Rapid7 repository was linked because it publishes a working exploit. The first Rapid7 commit is temporally after the firmware fix and adds only offensive modules, so treating it as either BIC or fix would invert causality. Public evidence closes the mechanism and fixed-version boundary (vulnerable below 1.0.7.81; fixed in 1.0.7.81), and demonstrates exploitability across releases at least as old as 1.0.4.128, but the vendor's source commit history is not present. Consequently the smallest true BIC, its immediate parent, the source-level fix SHA, and BIC commit-object AI signal cannot be established. This is a genuine unavailable-public-history boundary, so BLOCKED is appropriate rather than NOT_AI or an evidence-gap verdict based on the unrelated Metasploit commit.
remaining_gap: Grandstream's version-controlled source history for /app/bin/gs_web (or an authoritative source-commit mapping for firmware builds) is required to identify the smallest true BIC, directly verify its parent lacks the unsafe copy, identify the direct fix commit, determine the exact first affected release, and inspect the BIC commit object for AI markers. The public materials expose firmware binaries/release notes and a later Metasploit exploit, not that history.
